afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 112201
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
301 PM MST Sun Oct 11 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Lingering showers and an occasional storm this afternoon through
  tomorrow and tomorrow night with breezy south to southwest
  winds, strongest during the daylight hours.
  
- Temperatures cool through the start of the workweek with below
  normal reading anticipated through the middle of the week.

- Drier and quieter weather conditions develop by Wednesday and
  then breezy conditions may develop again by the end of the week.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
The remnant circulation of TC Rachel is no longer discernible on 
satellite, having sheared apart and fused with the large-scale 
trough across the West. However, showers and a few storms continue
to develop across AZ, feeding off elevated surface moisture (dew 
points in the upper 50s to lower 60s) and modest upslope ascent. A
lot of dry air has moved in aloft, especially above 700mb, which 
is choking the updrafts and, overall, showers are notably less 
intense than they were last night and early this morning. There 
has not been much in the way lightning either. Through the rest of
this afternoon and evening fast-moving showers and the occasional
thunderstorm are expected to continue to favor terrain areas of 
AZ, mainly north and east of Phoenix, and along a SSW-NNE oriented
band mostly between Phoenix and Quartzsite. The threat for 
localized flash flooding is all but over. With the fast-moving 
showers and lower intensity, it will be tough to accumulate enough
rainfall to lead to flash flooding. However, training of cells 
over the same areas may still lead to localized impacts. Latest 
REFS & HREF show the best potential for flooding impacts through 
this evening being in Yavapai County, associated with the band of 
continuous rain showers. Areas like Wickenburg have around a 
10-20% chance to pick up over 1" of rain this afternoon and 
evening.

In addition to the lingering rain showers this afternoon, winds 
have picked up across the region, associated with a strong 
pressure gradient. Surface wind gusts this afternoon have mostly 
been hitting 35-45 mph. Any shower, even weak ones, will be 
capable of mixing down stronger wind gusts to the surface. The 
gusty winds have also been strong enough to generate blowing dust 
and hazy skies in some areas. A Wind Advisory remains in effect 
through 5 PM this afternoon The gustiness should relax this 
evening with the loss of heating. It will be gusty again Monday, 
across mainly AZ, but the magnitude of gusts will be around 10-15 
kts lower than today.

Spotty showers and an occasional rumble of thunder are likely to 
continue into Monday, with a persistent southwest flow, especially
in the afternoon with surface heating. But again, the better rain
chances and coverage look to favor higher terrain areas of AZ and
in particular across Yavapai County. Steering winds will still be
very fast Monday, with 700-500mb winds around 30-60kts, which 
will limit rainfall totals. The REFS probability for rainfall 
Monday >0.25" is <20% south of I-10 to around 30-50% along the 
southern Yavapai County border. Rain chances are likely to improve
again going into Monday night - Tuesday morning as guidance shows
a shortwave trough, within the larger Western CONUS trough, 
clipping through the area. A weak cold front is also shown to move
west to east across the area, which may help focus showers and 
isolated storms into a scattered line/band. Once again, fast 
steering flow and overall low intensity showers should limit 
rainfall amounts with this activity Monday night to mostly under 
0.25" across the lower deserts. 

Temperatures will continue a downward trend through the start of 
the week, which is welcome news to just about everyone that 
grinded it out through another hot Summer+. Highs across southeast
CA today will mostly stay below 80 degrees while AZ locations 
have already warmed into the middle 80s. Temperatures are then 
forecast to cool several degrees into Monday, dropping ~5-8 
degrees with the lows and ~2-5 degrees with the highs. This 
cooling into Monday will be ahead of the weak cold front Monday 
night. So, further cooling is expected into Tuesday.

&&

.LONG TERM /TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/... 
Ensembles are in good agreement the Pacific low will slowly drift
east northeastward across far northern Arizona and southern Utah 
on Tuesday before most of the energy exits to the northeast on 
Wednesday. Additional dry air will spread across the region from 
the northwest during this time with PWATs dropping to 75% of 
normal and skies clearing out later on Tuesday. Behind the cold 
front on Tuesday, temperatures will dip further with NBM forecast 
highs only in the mid 70s Tuesday, or 10-15 degrees below normal. 
Overnight lows Tuesday night/Wednesday morning are also expected 
to fall well into the 50s for the bulk of the area to as cool as 
the mid to upper 40s for rural lower desert and higher terrain 
locations. 

Model guidance is still somewhat uncertain with the eventual 
placement of the incoming upper level ridge and a likely lingering
trough axis and/or cut-off low that should form late week. No 
matter the eventual evolution, our weather will basically stay the
same with dry conditions prevailing late week into next weekend. 
Temperatures will moderate some late week with highs returning 
into the 80s, but likely staying below normal. We may end up 
having another back-door cool front moving into the area from the 
east by Friday or Saturday and this should either maintain or cool
off temperatures going into next weekend. As with any backdoor 
front, gusty easterly winds are likely to follow as well and with 
the potential cutoff low in the area, easterly winds in this case
may become quite strong. Global models are already showing 
potential for some very strong, advisory level or higher, winds 
across southeast AZ.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1750Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:

The primary aviation weather concern during the TAF period will 
be gusty southerly cross-runway winds, with a secondary concern 
being periods of VCSH/SHRA conditions. Anticipate winds to prevail
out of S/SW'rly directions with gusts commonly between 25-30 kts 
and TEMPO higher gusts between 35-40 kts through 21-22Z. Winds 
will continue to gradually veer out of the SW and begin to relax 
heading into the evening. Late evening, confidence is moderate to 
good that winds will revert to SE and relax to AOB 12 kts. 
Tomorrow morning, winds will follow a similar pattern to what is 
observed today, gradually increasing and developing gusts while 
veering out of the south (and eventually SW by the afternoon), 
but with speeds nearly 10 kts lower than today. Northern portions
of the Phoenix airspace will continue to experience scattered
showers through the entire period, especially focused
along/towards higher terrain of Central AZ, leading to occasional
VCSH/SHRA conditions at the terminals. KDVT will have the best
chances given its closer proximity. Best timing for the next 
round of VCSH/SHRA will be mid afternoon through early evening.
Occasional, isolated lightning (TS) cannot be ruled out through
the period. Occasional VFR CIGs mostly above 6-7K ft AGL with 
FEW-SCT decks as low as 3-4K ft AGL can be expected.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:

Confidence is good that after a few more showers of lingering VCSH
conditions, a drier period will take hold. Winds will prevail out
of the SW/W with gusts to between 20-30 kts and briefly as high as
35 kts at times through mid afternoon. Speeds will relax below 15
kts late this afternoon with gusts mostly subsiding by this 
evening. Anticipate occasional CIGs above 7K ft AGL and otherwise
FEW-SCT midlevel decks through the period.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Isolated to scattered showers and a few storms will remain
possible across mainly AZ this afternoon through Monday night
before a weak cold front moves through and drier air filters in.
Winds will be strongest now/this afternoon, with gusts up to 35-45
mph from the S-SW. Gustiness will subside this evening and then
pick back up during the day Monday, but with magnitudes around
10-15 mph lower. Winds will then be lightest Tuesday and
Wednesday. Although a north to south gradient wind will develop
along the Lower Colorado River Wednesday, leading to some gusty
northerly winds. Winds then look to become stronger area-wide
Thursday and especially Friday into this weekend with a strong E-W
gradient potentially setting up. Drier conditions develop through
the day Tuesday and likely stay dry through the end of the week  
with MinRH values mostly between 40-60% the next couple days to
then 25-40% by Thursday. Below normal temperatures are expected
through at least the middle of the week.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Wind Advisory until 5 PM MST this afternoon for AZZ530>563.

CA...Wind Advisory until 5 PM PDT this afternoon for CAZ560>570.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Benedict
LONG TERM...Kuhlman/Benedict
AVIATION...Whittock 
FIRE WEATHER...Benedict
